newsitem.title: USA: Transition Systems sees Q4 similar to Q3.
newsitem.headline: Transition Systems sees Q4 similar to Q3.

text.p: Transition Systems Inc said on Monday it expects revenues and earnings for the fiscal fourth quarter ended September 30 to be comparable to the third quarter and higher than the year-ago fourth quarter.

Transition, a maker of healthcare management systems, made a proforma $0.15 per share in the third quarter on revenues of $10.1 million. In the year-ago fourth quarter it earned a proforma $0.11 a share on revenues of $9.04 million.
The stock was down almost 33 percent at 1015 EST/1515 GMT, to 9-1/2 from Friday's close of 13-3/4.

"We are pleased with the fourth quarter results, which led to full year-over-year revenue and earnings per share growth of approximately 25 percent and 55 percent, respectively," said Chief Executive Bob Raco.
Raco said these comparisons excluded the effects of a recapitalization in January 1996.
"(Order) Backlog increased by over 10 percent to a record high during the quarter, and the number of new deals in the pipeline is also at an all-time high," he said.
Revenue during the quarter was lower than expected because of some delay in closing a few contracts, he said, but added he saw no sign of weakness in the marketplace.
First Call's consensus estimate for the fourth quarter is $0.16 per share. The company is to release its results for the quarter on November 20.
